citations.description: test_a_flagged_attestation_is_REFUSED only asserts result is None, not that the verdict is named in the reply
Implementation does name the verdict in the refusal message, but the test does not assert this

findings.criterion: a `bugfix-size-attestation` block whose ticket attestation is absent or `stale-material` is still REFUSED, with the observed verdict named in the refusal reply
findings.detail: The test `test_a_flagged_attestation_is_REFUSED` only asserts `result is None` — it does not check that the observed verdict is named in the refusal reply. The implementation does append the verdict to the refusal message (retrigger.py:243-244, `if detail and detail.startswith("attestation-"): base += f" (attestation re-check: {detail})"`), but the acceptance criterion explicitly requires this to be asserted by a test, and no test verifies the reply content for the flagged-attestation case.

citations.description: Only unresolvable ticket id and classifier exception are individually tested; missing header, unparseable count, and missing criterion line are not
sole_blocking_criterion handles all parse failure cases but missing header and missing criterion line are not individually tested

findings.criterion: every parse failure refuses: missing header, unparseable count, missing criterion line, unresolvable ticket id, classifier exception — each asserted, not assumed
findings.detail: The criterion explicitly requires each parse failure case to be individually asserted. Tests exist for unresolvable ticket id (`test_an_unresolvable_ticket_REFUSES`) and classifier exception (`test_the_classifier_raising_REFUSES`), but there are no tests for: (1) missing header in the bot vote message, (2) unparseable count (though the implementation marks this `pragma: no cover` as unreachable), and (3) missing criterion line (a message with a valid count=1 header but no `- (...)` line). The criterion says 'each asserted, not assumed' — three of the five cases are not individually asserted.

data.remediation: How to resolve the unmet criteria: for each one, decide whether the work is genuinely incomplete or simply undocumented. The completion verifier reads this ticket's comments, so evidence you record there is taken into account on the next verification. For any criterion whose work is genuinely unfinished, complete it, then re-verify.
